doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Joining the musicians' union
summary: He joined at eighteen after a token reading test and sees little union help.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Were you a member of the musician’s union at this time?

Yeah I joined when I was eighteen. And it was a joke almost. I got in there and they said — they handed me a piece of music which was Schubert’s “Serenade,” which I’d played five years earlier. I sat down and I went [scats]. That’s all right. Okay. That’s enough. So I could read whatever was put there. Kind of silly
“Give me the money and pay your dues and you’re a member.” A joke.
Have they ever come to bat for you over the years?
For what? I don’t know. I wouldn’t know what to complain about.
